story.title: Supreme Court Denies Trump's Appeal in E. Jean Carroll Case
story.summary: The Supreme Court has rejected President Donald Trump's appeal regarding a $5 million verdict awarded to E. Jean Carroll. This decision marks the second time the Court has declined to hear Trump's request to overturn the jury's finding of liability for sexual abuse and defamation against Carroll.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed after the Court's denial?
explore_lenses.title: The $5 million case has reached its endpoint
explore_lenses.summary: The August 17 action was a denial of Trump’s request for rehearing, not a new ruling on the evidence. It leaves intact the 2023 jury verdict and the lower-court decisions that upheld it.

claims.text: The Supreme Court first denied Trump’s certiorari petition on June 29, 2026, and denied his rehearing petition on August 17, 2026.
The 2023 verdict found Trump liable for sexually abusing Carroll and for defaming her in a 2022 denial; the Court’s refusal to review or rehear the appeal leaves that judgment undisturbed.
Carroll’s lawyer, Roberta Kaplan, said the result makes the jury verdict final and no longer challengeable in court; Trump continues to deny wrongdoing.

explore_lenses.label: Has Carroll already received the money?
explore_lenses.title: Yes; the escrowed award was released in July
explore_lenses.summary: The Supreme Court’s action does not trigger a new payment process: the judgment funds were already released after the Court’s June 29 denial. Interest increased the amount above the original jury award.

claims.text: Court records and Carroll’s counsel said Carroll received nearly $5.63 million on July 14, 2026—the $5 million verdict plus accrued interest—from funds Trump had placed in escrow.

Before the disbursement, Trump’s lawyers sought to keep the money in escrow, arguing that releasing it could cause irreparable harm if the judgment were later reversed; Judge Lewis Kaplan found that scenario highly unlikely, according to Reuters reporting.

explore_lenses.label: What remains unresolved in Carroll's other case?
explore_lenses.title: A separate $83.3 million appeal is still pending
explore_lenses.summary: This decision concerns the 2023 $5 million sexual-abuse and 2022-defamation verdict. A different case over Trump’s 2019 statements about Carroll and an $83.3 million defamation judgment remains before the Supreme Court.

claims.text: Trump’s separate petition, docketed as No. 26-141 on July 30, 2026, challenges the $83.3 million judgment; Carroll’s response is due August 31, 2026, and the Court had not acted on it as of August 18.

Trump argues that his 2019 White House statements denying Carroll’s allegation were official presidential acts protected by immunity, that he did not waive that immunity, and that the United States should have been substituted as defendant under the Westfall Act.
AP reports that Trump and the Justice Department are asking the Court to overturn the second verdict on immunity grounds.

story_report.summary: The Supreme Court on Aug. 17 denied Donald Trump’s petition for rehearing in his challenge to E. Jean Carroll’s $5 million jury award. The court had already declined to take up his appeal on June 29. Its refusal to review or rehear the case leaves undisturbed the 2023 verdict finding Trump liable for sexually abusing Carroll and defaming her in a 2022 denial, according to Carroll’s lawyer and reporting on the case.

sections.heading: Carroll Verdict and Court Review
sections.body: The $5 million verdict stemmed from a 2023 jury finding that Trump was liable for sexual abuse and defamation. The defamation finding concerned a 2022 denial of Carroll’s allegation. Carroll’s lawyer, Roberta Kaplan, said the Supreme Court’s action makes the judgment final and no longer challengeable in court, while Trump continues to deny wrongdoing.

sections.heading: Escrow Funds Paid to Carroll
sections.body: Carroll received nearly $5.63 million on July 14, including the $5 million verdict and accrued interest, from funds Trump had placed in escrow, according to court records and her counsel. Before the payment, Trump’s lawyers argued the money should remain in escrow because releasing it could cause irreparable harm if the judgment were reversed; Judge Lewis Kaplan found that outcome highly unlikely, Reuters reported.

sections.heading: Separate $83.3 Million Appeal
sections.body: A separate Trump petition challenging an $83.3 million judgment remains pending at the Supreme Court. Docketed as No. 26-141 on July 30, it argues that Trump’s 2019 White House denials were official acts protected by presidential immunity, that the immunity was not waived, and that the United States should have been substituted as defendant under the Westfall Act. Carroll’s response is due Aug. 31.

unresolved.text: It remains unresolved whether the Supreme Court will grant review of Trump’s separate appeal in No. 26-141; the deadline for Carroll’s response does not indicate whether the court will take the case.

related_stories.title: Kushner Engages in Middle East Talks to Revive Gaza Peace Plan Amid Israeli Resistance
related_stories.summary: Jared Kushner, the US envoy, is on a diplomatic mission in the Middle East, meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Hamas officials to revive a stalled peace plan for Gaza. This effort follows Netanyahu's recent rejection of a US-backed 15-point peace plan, marking a significant divergence from the Trump administration's approach. Kushner indicated that progress towards disarming Hamas could potentially begin within 30 days.

related_stories.title: Hakainde Hichilema Secures Re-election in Zambia with 60% of Votes
related_stories.summary: Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema has been re-elected, receiving approximately 60% of the votes in the recent presidential election, according to the electoral commission. The election was perceived as a referendum on his first term, during which the country's economy began to recover after a period of fiscal challenges. However, the election was marred by reports of government actions against opposition figures on election night.
